The placode is described as a focal thickening of the epidermal layer; histologically it is seen as budding of basal cells at 14-15 PCW, and its formation is accompanied by invagination into the dermis.
quotes: epidermal placodes (focal sites of epidermal layer thickening)
At 14-15 PCW, budding of basal cells (hair placode and germ cells) and elongation of HFs (hair pegs) were observed
The Dc, for which formation is accompanied by invagination of the placode
judge_why: Gives focal epidermal thickening, budding of basal cells and invagination, matching the intended answer.

reader_answer: The placode is an epidermal/epithelial structure in the basal epidermis of prenatal skin, appearing as budding basal cells from 14-15 PCW, and it is abutted by the dermal condensate beneath it.
quotes: At 14-15 PCW, budding of basal cells (hair placode and germ cells) and elongation of HFs (hair pegs) were observed
aggregate to form the Dc (FOXD1+SOX2+), which abuts the epithelial hair placode

we identified HF cells from 14 PCW in our scRNA-seq data, which comprised placode, matrix (SHH+), outer root sheath (ORS) (SLC26A7+), companion layer (CL), inner root sheath (IRS) and cuticle and cortex cells
judge_why: Places the placode in the epidermis/basal epidermis with the dermal condensate abutting it from below.

reader_answer: The placode initiates hair follicle formation through interaction with the dermal condensate, and it gives rise to hair matrix cells; it lies on the IRS differentiation trajectory and receives migration/invasion-promoting signals from the Dc.
quotes: Prenatal HFs start forming between 11 and 14 post-conception weeks (PCW), initiated by interactions between epidermal placodes (focal sites of epidermal layer thickening) and dermal condensates (aggregates of dermal fibroblasts)
We evaluated hair matrix cells, which arise from the epidermal placode, a prenatal-specific cell state absent in established adult HFs
IRS trajectory, involving placode, matrix, cuticle/cortex and IRS
judge_why: States initiation of hair follicle formation with the dermal condensate and origin of hair matrix cells; extra trajectory detail is additive.

reader_answer: The supplied context does not give marker genes for the hair placode. It names markers for neighbouring HF states (for example matrix SHH+, ORS SLC26A7+) and receptors said to be on the placode (LAMP1, CXADR, EPHB6), but no genes are presented as marking the placode itself.
The paper identifies macrophage subsets by marker genes rather than giving pan-macrophage markers: LYVE1+, MHCII+, TREM2+ microglia-like (TREM2, P2RY12, CX3CR1, OLFML3) and iron-recycling subsets.
quotes: the four macrophage subsets (LYVE1+, MHCII+, TML and iron-recycling) expressed gene programs that drive angiogenesis

We recently identified yolk-sac derived TREM2+ macrophages that share an expression profile (P2RY12, CX3CR1 and OLFML3) with microglia-like macrophages from other developing organs, such as the brain, prenatal skin and gonads
judge_why: Correctly handles the broad label by giving per-subset markers including MHCII and the TREM2/P2RY12/CX3CR1/OLFML3 microglia-like set.

reader_answer: Macrophages seed the skin from as early as 6 PCW and are present throughout gestation, co-locating with endothelial and neural cells in early and late neurovascular microenvironments (ME1 and ME5) and, for the LYVE1+ subset, with WNT2+ dermal fibroblasts.
quotes: immune cells such as macrophages seed the skin as early as 6 PCW and express a range of pro-inflammatory genes
Macrophages co-located with endothelial and neural cells in 'early and late neurovascular microenvironments' (ME1 and ME5, respectively)
Specifically, LYVE1+ macrophages co-located with WNT2+ fibroblasts (Fig. 3c-e)
judge_why: Names seeding from 6 PCW and co-location with endothelial/neural cells in ME1 and ME5, plus fibroblast co-location.

reader_answer: Macrophages are proposed to support skin morphogenesis: maintaining dermal fibroblasts, contributing to scarless repair, supporting peripheral nerve development, and driving angiogenesis and vascular network remodelling (shown by adding iPS-derived macrophages to skin organoids).
quotes: Our atlas indicated that macrophages contribute to scarless skin repair, fibroblast homeostasis and neurovascular development.

Our identification of additional growth factor interactions (IGF1-IGF1R and GRN-EGFR) (Extended Data Fig. 7g and Supplementary Table 8) suggests that LYVE1+ macrophages play a part in the maintenance of prenatal skin dermal fibroblasts.
These findings suggest that prenatal skin macrophages may support the establishment of the skin peripheral nervous system during early gestation, as previously reported in mouse skin.
Collectively, our findings demonstrate that interactions between macrophages and endothelial cells are required to support angiogenesis through blood vessel remodelling.
judge_why: Covers angiogenesis/vessel remodelling, scarless repair, fibroblast homeostasis and neural development.

reader_answer: Beyond WNT2 itself, the paper reports genes differentially expressed by this subset: late-gestation WNT2+ fibroblasts upregulate COL1A1, early ones SFRP1, and the subset expresses CDKN1A, IL1R1 and POSTN, with downregulated IL6 relative to adult fibroblasts.
quotes: Late gestation WNT2+ fibroblasts had upregulated genes related to extracellular matrix and collagen deposition (for example, COL1A1), whereas early WNT2+ fibroblasts had DEGs involved in cellular growth and differentiation (for example, SFRP1)
Notably, WNT2+ and PEAR1+ prenatal fibroblasts expressed several genes involved in cellular senescence (CDKN1A), cytokine pathways (for example, IL1R1) and collagen deposition (for example, POSTN)
judge_why: Reports WNT2, late COL1A1/ECM, early SFRP1, plus CDKN1A, IL1R1, POSTN and downregulated IL6.

reader_answer: WNT2+ fibroblasts are dermal fibroblasts of prenatal skin that become abundant in later gestation; they co-locate with LYVE1+ macrophages and, in early prenatal skin (6-8 PCW), with TML macrophages.
quotes: The adult fibroblast gene expression profile was increased in WNT2+ and PEAR1+ prenatal fibroblasts, which were abundant in later gestation
Specifically, LYVE1+ macrophages co-located with WNT2+ fibroblasts (Fig. 3c-e)
TML macrophages were predicted to co-locate with WNT2+ fibroblasts in early prenatal skin (6-8 PCW) (Fig. 3c,d)
judge_why: Dermal, co-locating with LYVE1+ macrophages and with TML macrophages at 6-8 PCW, as intended.

reader_answer: WNT2+ fibroblasts form the dermal fibroblast branch of the fibroblast trajectory and shift function across gestation: early cells express growth and differentiation genes, whereas late cells deposit extracellular matrix and collagen and express senescence/cytokine genes characteristic of pathogenic fibrotic fibroblasts, linking them to the loss of scarless healing.
quotes: the second (dermal fibroblast trajectory) formed WNT2+ fibroblasts and PEAR1+ fibroblasts (abundant after 11 PCW)

Late gestation WNT2+ fibroblasts had upregulated genes related to extracellular matrix and collagen deposition (for example, COL1A1), whereas early WNT2+ fibroblasts had DEGs involved in cellular growth and differentiation (for example, SFRP1)

Notably, WNT2+ and PEAR1+ prenatal fibroblasts expressed several genes involved in cellular senescence (CDKN1A), cytokine pathways (for example, IL1R1) and collagen deposition (for example, POSTN) (Fig. 3a,b), which are highly expressed in pathogenic fibroblasts of fibrotic skin disorders.
were predicted to interact through platelet-derived growth factors (PDGFs) and corresponding receptors (PDGFRα and PDGFRβ) expressed on fibroblasts
judge_why: Captures the early growth/differentiation to late ECM-collagen shift and acquisition of a senescent, pro-inflammatory adult-like profile.

reader_answer: TML macrophages are TREM2+ and share a microglial expression profile of P2RY12, CX3CR1 and OLFML3; they also co-express immunomodulatory genes such as CX3CR1 and SYT11, and express GAS6.
quotes: We recently identified yolk-sac derived TREM2+ macrophages that share an expression profile (P2RY12, CX3CR1 and OLFML3) with microglia-like macrophages from other developing organs
co-expressed immunomodulatory genes, including immune-inhibitory receptors (for example, CX3CR1) and regulators of IL-6 production (for example, SYT11)
judge_why: Gives TREM2 with P2RY12, CX3CR1, OLFML3 and GAS6, matching the intended marker set.

reader_answer: TML macrophages are found in early prenatal skin, where they are predicted to co-locate with WNT2+ fibroblasts (6-8 PCW) and with Schwann cells in the early neurovascular microenvironment (ME1), and are seen close to endothelial cells.
quotes: TML macrophages were predicted to co-locate with WNT2+ fibroblasts in early prenatal skin (6-8 PCW) (Fig. 3c,d)
TML macrophages were also predicted to co-locate with Schwann cells in prenatal skin ('early neurovascular microenvironment', ME1) (Figs. 1d and 3g)
multiplex RNAscope and immunofluorescence staining showed LYVE1+ and TML macrophages in close proximity to endothelial cells
judge_why: Names WNT2+ fibroblast co-location at 6-8 PCW, Schwann cells in ME1, and proximity to endothelial cells.

reader_answer: TML macrophages are yolk-sac derived, microglia-like cells implicated in immunomodulation and anti-fibrogenic/scarless healing (IL-6 regulation, GAS6-AXL signalling to fibroblasts), in supporting cutaneous neural development via interactions with Schwann cells, and in promoting sprouting angiogenesis.
quotes: co-expressed immunomodulatory genes, including immune-inhibitory receptors (for example, CX3CR1) and regulators of IL-6 production (for example, SYT11)

Additionally, GAS6, expressed by TML macrophages and LYVE1+ macrophages, was predicted to interact with AXL receptors on WNT2+ fibroblasts (Extended Data Fig. 7g and Supplementary Table 8), and these interactions can induce immunosuppression and tissue repair
TML macrophages were predicted to interact with Schwann cells, contributing to synapse formation and axon guidance (VEGFA-NRP1, VEGFA-NRP2, SEMA3C-NRP2 and SEMA3E-PLXND1)
Gene module expression profiles suggested that sprouting angiogenesis (growth of new vessels) was promoted by LYVE1+ and TML macrophages
judge_why: Includes sprouting angiogenesis and the Schwann cell interaction for synapse formation and axon guidance; other roles are additive, not contradictory.

reader_answer: The dermal condensate is annotated as FOXD1+SOX2+ (arising from PDGFRA+FOXD1+SOX2low pre-Dc cells) and expresses FAM3C and EFNB1, with COL6A3, MFAP4 and PTK7 expressed as pre-Dc cells aggregate into the Dc.
quotes: In mice, transitional PDGFRA+FOXD1+SOX2low fibroblasts termed pre-Dc cells aggregate to form the Dc (FOXD1+SOX2+), which abuts the epithelial hair placode
The Dc, for which formation is accompanied by invagination of the placode, expressed FAM3C and EFNB1
Genes implicated in collagen fibril formation and cell adhesion (COL6A3, MFAP4 and PTK7) were expressed as the pre-Dc cells aggregated into the Dc
judge_why: Gives FOXD1+SOX2+ with the PDGFRA+FOXD1+SOX2low pre-Dc precursor and FAM3C/EFNB1.

reader_answer: The Dc sits in the dermal compartment of prenatal skin from 12 PCW, as a hair-follicle-specialized fibroblast aggregate abutting the epithelial hair placode; after invagination it becomes encapsulated at the follicle base as the dermal papilla.
quotes: Within the dermal compartment, we observed HF-specialized fibroblasts, the dermal condensate (Dc) and dermal papilla (Dp), from 12 PCW (Extended Data Fig. 3c).
In mice, transitional PDGFRA+FOXD1+SOX2low fibroblasts termed pre-Dc cells aggregate to form the Dc (FOXD1+SOX2+), which abuts the epithelial hair placode,.
Following HF invagination, the Dc becomes encapsulated at its base as the Dp (NDP+, SOX2+), (Fig. 2c and Extended Data Fig. 3h).
judge_why: Dermal compartment from 12 PCW abutting the epithelial hair placode, as intended.

reader_answer: The Dc participates in mesenchymal-epithelial crosstalk driving hair follicle formation: its formation accompanies placode invagination, and it expresses FAM3C and EFNB1 predicted to signal to receptors on the placode and reported to promote cell migration and invasion. Prenatal hair follicle formation more broadly is initiated by interactions between epidermal placodes and dermal condensates.
quotes: The Dc, for which formation is accompanied by invagination of the placode, expressed FAM3C and EFNB1, which were, respectively, predicted to interact with LAMP1 or CXADR and EPHB6 on the placode, and have been reported to promote cell migration and invasion, (Fig. 2g, Extended Data Fig. 5b and Supplementary Table 8).

Prenatal HFs start forming between 11 and 14 post-conception weeks (PCW), initiated by interactions between epidermal placodes (focal sites of epidermal layer thickening) and dermal condensates (aggregates of dermal fibroblasts), whereas sebaceous glands develop from around 16 PCW.
judge_why: Conveys Dc-placode crosstalk driving hair follicle formation and the FAM3C/EFNB1 migration-invasion point.

reader_answer: Matrix cells are identified as SHH+, with SHH and WNT10B described as known matrix markers upregulated along the IRS trajectory. Relative to adult hair follicles, prenatal matrix cells also show increased CXCL14 and CD24 expression.
quotes: Consistent with our histological observations, we identified HF cells from 14 PCW in our scRNA-seq data, which comprised placode, matrix (SHH+), outer root sheath (ORS) (SLC26A7+), companion layer (CL), inner root sheath (IRS) and cuticle and cortex cells (cuticle/cortex; part of the inner layers of the HF) (Fig. 2a-c, Extended Data Fig. 3a,b and Supplementary Table 6).
AGR2 was downregulated along the IRS trajectory, whereas known matrix markers such as SHH and WNT10B, were upregulated (Extended Data Fig. 4b,c and Supplementary Table 7).

Compared with adult HFs, prenatal skin matrix cells had increased expression of genes involved in chemotaxis, such as CXCL14, a chemokine previously reported to recruit regulatory T (Treg) cells, and in control of autoimmunity (CD24).
judge_why: Names SHH and WNT10B as the known matrix markers, correctly scoped to hair matrix.

reader_answer: Matrix cells are hair follicle epithelial cells detected in prenatal skin from 14 PCW; they arise from the epidermal placode and lie overlying the dermal papilla. They are a prenatal-specific state absent from established adult hair follicles.
quotes: Consistent with our histological observations, we identified HF cells from 14 PCW in our scRNA-seq data, which comprised placode, matrix (SHH+), outer root sheath (ORS) (SLC26A7+), companion layer (CL), inner root sheath (IRS) and cuticle and cortex cells (cuticle/cortex; part of the inner layers of the HF) (Fig. 2a-c, Extended Data Fig. 3a,b and Supplementary Table 6).
We evaluated hair matrix cells, which arise from the epidermal placode, a prenatal-specific cell state absent in established adult HFs (Extended Data Fig. 3d,e).

Finally, RSPO3 from the Dp was predicted to interact with LGR4 and LGR6 (Fig. 2g, Extended Data Fig. 5b and Supplementary Table 8) in overlying matrix cells to contribute to the proliferation of HF epithelial cells.
judge_why: Hair follicle, arising from the epidermal placode, prenatal-specific and from 14 PCW - all present.

reader_answer: Matrix cells differentiate along the IRS trajectory towards cuticle/cortex and inner root sheath, and prenatal matrix cells express chemotactic and immune-regulatory genes (CXCL14, CD24) suggesting a role in Treg cell recruitment and immune protection during early matrix differentiation. Their differentiation is coordinated by Dp-derived signals (RSPO3, WNT5A), with RSPO3-LGR4/LGR6 contributing to proliferation of hair follicle epithelial cells.
quotes: Compared with adult HFs, prenatal skin matrix cells had increased expression of genes involved in chemotaxis, such as CXCL14, a chemokine previously reported to recruit regulatory T (Treg) cells, and in control of autoimmunity (CD24). This result highlighted the potential role of Treg cell accumulation and immune protection in the early stages of matrix differentiation (Extended Data Fig. 3f).
Formation of the Dp was characterized by genes (RSPO3 and WNT5A) (Extended Data Fig. 4f and Supplementary Table 7) that coordinate the differentiation of adjacent hair matrix cells,.

Finally, RSPO3 from the Dp was predicted to interact with LGR4 and LGR6 (Fig. 2g, Extended Data Fig. 5b and Supplementary Table 8) in overlying matrix cells to contribute to the proliferation of HF epithelial cells.
judge_why: Gives the CXCL14/CD24 chemotaxis and Treg immune-protection role; added differentiation detail is also supported.

reader_answer: The subset is named for LYVE1 expression and is one of four prenatal skin macrophage subsets; the only other gene the context states it expresses is GAS6 (shared with TML macrophages). No full marker panel is given.
quotes: Gene ontology analysis showed that the four macrophage subsets (LYVE1+, MHCII+, TML and iron-recycling) expressed gene programs that drive angiogenesis (Supplementary Tables 23-26).

Additionally, GAS6, expressed by TML macrophages and LYVE1+ macrophages, was predicted to interact with AXL receptors on WNT2+ fibroblasts (Extended Data Fig. 7g and Supplementary Table 8), and these interactions can induce immunosuppression and tissue repair,.
judge_why: Identifies LYVE1 and GAS6 and correctly flags that no full marker panel is in the text.

reader_answer: LYVE1+ macrophages are found in prenatal skin co-located with WNT2+ fibroblasts, and imaging placed LYVE1+ macrophages in close proximity to endothelial cells; macrophage subsets more generally were predicted to co-locate with fibroblasts, neural cells and vascular cells in distinct microenvironments in early gestation.
quotes: Specifically, LYVE1+ macrophages co-located with WNT2+ fibroblasts (Fig. 3c-e) and were predicted to interact through platelet-derived growth factors (PDGFs) and corresponding receptors (PDGFRα and PDGFRβ) expressed on fibroblasts (Extended Data Fig. 7g and Supplementary Table 8).
Consistent with this finding, multiplex RNAscope and immunofluorescence staining showed LYVE1+ and TML macrophages in close proximity to endothelial cells (Fig. 4a and Supplementary Video 1).

In prenatal skin, macrophage subsets (Extended Data Fig. 7e,f) were predicted to co-locate with fibroblasts, neural cells and vascular cells in distinct tissue microenvironments in early gestation (Fig. 1d).
judge_why: Co-location with WNT2+ fibroblasts and imaging proximity to endothelial cells both given.

reader_answer: LYVE1+ macrophages are proposed to maintain prenatal skin dermal fibroblasts through PDGF, IGF1-IGF1R and GRN-EGFR interactions, and to promote angiogenesis - specifically sprouting angiogenesis and blood vessel morphogenesis. Their GAS6 is predicted to engage AXL on WNT2+ fibroblasts, an interaction linked to immunosuppression and tissue repair.
quotes: Our identification of additional growth factor interactions (IGF1-IGF1R and GRN-EGFR) (Extended Data Fig. 7g and Supplementary Table 8) suggests that LYVE1+ macrophages play a part in the maintenance of prenatal skin dermal fibroblasts.

Gene module expression profiles suggested that sprouting angiogenesis (growth of new vessels) was promoted by LYVE1+ and TML macrophages, blood vessel morphogenesis by LYVE1+ macrophages and endothelial cell chemotaxis by iron-recycling macrophages (Extended Data Fig. 8i and Supplementary Table 27).

Additionally, GAS6, expressed by TML macrophages and LYVE1+ macrophages, was predicted to interact with AXL receptors on WNT2+ fibroblasts (Extended Data Fig. 7g and Supplementary Table 8), and these interactions can induce immunosuppression and tissue repair,.
judge_why: Sprouting angiogenesis, vessel morphogenesis and fibroblast maintenance via PDGF and GAS6-AXL all conveyed.

reader_answer: Prenatal skin fibroblast subsets are defined by HOXC5 (early fibroblasts), WNT2, PEAR1 and FRZB; hair-specialized fibroblasts are marked by PDGFRA/FOXD1/SOX2low (pre-Dc), FOXD1+SOX2+ (Dc) and NDP+SOX2+ (Dp). Human prenatal fibroblasts did not significantly express the papillary fibroblast marker COL13A1.
quotes: Inferred trajectory analysis predicted that HOXC5+ early fibroblasts (located in the upper dermis (Fig. 2f) and abundant before 11 PCW (Extended Data Fig. 3c)) differentiated along two paths: the first (hair fibroblast trajectory) formed hair-specialized fibroblasts (pre-Dc cells, the Dc and Dp) and the second (dermal fibroblast trajectory) formed WNT2+ fibroblasts and PEAR1+ fibroblasts (abundant after 11 PCW) (Fig. 2e, Extended Data Figs. 3c and 4d and Supplementary Table 7).
In mice, transitional PDGFRA+FOXD1+SOX2low fibroblasts termed pre-Dc cells aggregate to form the Dc (FOXD1+SOX2+), which abuts the epithelial hair placode,.
Following HF invagination, the Dc becomes encapsulated at its base as the Dp (NDP+, SOX2+), (Fig. 2c and Extended Data Fig. 3h).

Our human prenatal skin fibroblasts did not significantly express papillary fibroblast markers (for example, COL13A1) (Extended Data Fig. 5j), which suggested that the distinction between papillary and reticular fibroblasts emerges after 17 PCW.
judge_why: Subset-specific marker answer is licensed by the hazard note and it captures the COL13A1-negative point.

reader_answer: Fibroblasts are dermal cells: HOXC5+ early fibroblasts sit in the upper dermis, and hair-specialized fibroblasts (Dc, Dp) are found in the dermal compartment from 12 PCW; dermal condensates are aggregates of dermal fibroblasts abutting the epidermal placode. Mesoderm-derived cells including skin fibroblasts are present throughout gestation.
quotes: Inferred trajectory analysis predicted that HOXC5+ early fibroblasts (located in the upper dermis (Fig. 2f) and abundant before 11 PCW (Extended Data Fig. 3c)) differentiated along two paths: the first (hair fibroblast trajectory) formed hair-specialized fibroblasts (pre-Dc cells, the Dc and Dp) and the second (dermal fibroblast trajectory) formed WNT2+ fibroblasts and PEAR1+ fibroblasts (abundant after 11 PCW) (Fig. 2e, Extended Data Figs. 3c and 4d and Supplementary Table 7).
Within the dermal compartment, we observed HF-specialized fibroblasts, the dermal condensate (Dc) and dermal papilla (Dp), from 12 PCW (Extended Data Fig. 3c).
Mesoderm-derived cells, including skin fibroblasts and endothelial cells, and immune cells were present throughout gestation (Fig. 1c, Extended Data Fig. 1d and Supplementary Table 4).
judge_why: Dermal compartment, HOXC5+ in upper dermis, Dc/Dp from 12 PCW - matches intended.

reader_answer: Fibroblasts produce the collagen whose aggregation causes scars, and prenatal fibroblasts instead upregulate immune suppression, inflammation regulation and tissue regeneration genes, which may favour scarless healing before they progressively acquire scar-promoting, pro-inflammatory profiles in later gestation. Hair-specialized fibroblasts also drive hair follicle morphogenesis through crosstalk with epidermal cells, including CXCL12-ACKR3-mediated pre-Dc migration.
quotes: Scars result from aggregation of collagen produced by dermal fibroblasts and failure of the overlying epidermis to completely regenerate.

By contrast, prenatal skin fibroblasts had upregulated genes involved in immune suppression (CD200), regulation of inflammation (for example, RAMP2) and tissue regeneration (MDK) (Fig. 3a and Supplementary Tables 13-15).

Collectively, our findings suggest that prenatal skin fibroblasts in early gestation downregulate genes involved in extracellular matrix formation, collagen deposition and inflammation, which may favour tissue regeneration over scarring.
We delineated the dermal cell types involved in crosstalk with epidermal cells during HF development and captured the precursors of the human Dc (Extended Data Figs. 2b and 3c).
judge_why: States the regeneration-over-scarring conclusion with the ECM/collagen/inflammation downregulation.

reader_answer: Periderm is an ectoderm-derived immature interfollicular epidermal cell type of prenatal skin, present from 7 PCW and enriched in early gestation; it overlies the dermal stroma as part of the epidermal layer and is seen sloughing from 11 PCW.
quotes: Among ectoderm-derived cells, neural cells and the periderm, which constitutes the first skin permeability barrier, were enriched in early gestation, whereas suprabasal epidermal and HF cells were mainly observed in later gestation (Fig. 1c, Extended Data Fig. 1d and Supplementary Table 4).
Prenatal skin up to 8 PCW consisted of a layer of epidermal cells overlying the dermal stroma, with the periderm seen sloughing from 11 PCW (Fig. 2a).
Immature IFE cells, including periderm, immature basal and immature suprabasal cells, were present from 7 PCW and decreased after 11 PCW, during the transition from embryonic to fetal skin (Fig. 2b).
judge_why: Outermost epidermal layer over dermal stroma, from 7 PCW, sloughing from 11 PCW.

reader_answer: The periderm constitutes the first skin permeability barrier.
quotes: Among ectoderm-derived cells, neural cells and the periderm, which constitutes the first skin permeability barrier, were enriched in early gestation, whereas suprabasal epidermal and HF cells were mainly observed in later gestation (Fig. 1c, Extended Data Fig. 1d and Supplementary Table 4).
judge_why: Exactly the first skin permeability barrier.

reader_answer: The only morphological statement is histological: the periderm is seen sloughing from 11 PCW, above the layer of epidermal cells overlying the dermal stroma; it is classed as an immature interfollicular epidermal cell state. No further structural description is given.
quotes: Prenatal skin up to 8 PCW consisted of a layer of epidermal cells overlying the dermal stroma, with the periderm seen sloughing from 11 PCW (Fig. 2a).
Immature IFE cells, including periderm, immature basal and immature suprabasal cells, were present from 7 PCW and decreased after 11 PCW, during the transition from embryonic to fetal skin (Fig. 2b).
judge_why: Gives the layer description and sloughing observation and notes nothing further is said.

reader_answer: HOXC5+ early fibroblasts are located in the upper dermis and are abundant before 11 PCW.
quotes: HOXC5+ early fibroblasts (located in the upper dermis (Fig. 2f) and abundant before 11 PCW (Extended Data Fig. 3c))
judge_why: Upper dermis, as intended.

reader_answer: They act as a common fibroblast progenitor, differentiating along a hair fibroblast trajectory (pre-Dc, Dc and Dp) and a dermal fibroblast trajectory (WNT2+ and PEAR1+ fibroblasts).
quotes: Inferred trajectory analysis predicted that HOXC5+ early fibroblasts (located in the upper dermis (Fig. 2f) and abundant before 11 PCW (Extended Data Fig. 3c)) differentiated along two paths: the first (hair fibroblast trajectory) formed hair-specialized fibroblasts (pre-Dc cells, the Dc and Dp) and the second (dermal fibroblast trajectory) formed WNT2+ fibroblasts and PEAR1+ fibroblasts (abundant after 11 PCW)
pre-Dcs, the Dc and Dp and dermal fibroblasts in human prenatal skin also originated from a common fibroblast progenitor (HOXC5+ early fibroblast)
judge_why: States the common fibroblast progenitor role and both trajectories exactly as intended.

reader_answer: Mature basal interfollicular epidermal cells are marked by DPYSL2, and AGR2 is newly identified as upregulated by DPYSL2+ basal cells along the ORS/CL trajectory.
quotes: Mature basal (DPYSL2+) and suprabasal IFE cells increased after 11 PCW
we identified new genes upregulated by DPYSL2+ basal cells, such as AGR2, and previously reported genes related to ORS differentiation (BARX2 and SOX9)
judge_why: Gives DPYSL2 and AGR2 as the newly identified gene without claiming BARX2/SOX9 as new.

reader_answer: DPYSL2+ basal cells are an intermediate state on the ORS/CL differentiation trajectory downstream of POSTN+ basal cells, upregulating AGR2 and genes related to outer root sheath differentiation.
quotes: predicted the differentiation of POSTN+ basal cells into two paths: ORS/CL trajectory, comprising DPYSL2+ basal cells, ORS and CL
we identified new genes upregulated by DPYSL2+ basal cells, such as AGR2, and previously reported genes related to ORS differentiation (BARX2 and SOX9)
judge_why: Places the cell type on the ORS/CL trajectory downstream of POSTN+ basal cells as intended.
